skillMdInspector.config.general.title: General
skillMdInspector.config.general.timeForm: Time format for the "Generated" timestamp shown in generated reports. "european" uses a 24-hour clock; "usa" uses a 12-hour clock with AM/PM.
skillMdInspector.config.validation.title: Validation
skillMdInspector.config.validation.enabl: Enable deterministic validation of SKILL.md files.
skillMdInspector.config.validation.runOn: Re-run validation whenever a SKILL.md file is saved.
skillMdInspector.config.tokens.maxCounte: Largest bundled resource file that is read and token-counted, in kilobytes. Files above this are skipped and excluded from the token report; counting has to read and BPE-encode the whole file, so an unbounded one can stall analysis.
skillMdInspector.config.validation.compa: Include the specification baseline (skills-ref) in the agent compatibility projection.
Include Claude Code in the agent compatibility projection.
Include Codex in the agent compatibility projection.
Include OpenCode in the agent compatibility projection.
How strictly to surface advisory body-section recommendations (examples, when-to-use, etc.). "off" disables them; "recommended" uses information-level diagnostics; "strict" uses warnings. Structural body errors are unaffected.
skillMdInspector.config.description.lang: Language used by description heuristics. "en" forces English analysis; "auto" marks the quality score as language-limited when it detects a non-Latin script (Cyrillic, CJK, …) or a common Latin-script language (German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese) via stopword profiles. Other languages may still be scored as English.
skillMdInspector.config.description.maxL: Maximum allowed length of the description field.
skillMdInspector.config.description.minL: Minimum recommended length of the description field.
skillMdInspector.config.name.maxLength.d: Maximum allowed length of the name field.
skillMdInspector.config.collision.bounda: How strongly mutually-exclusive "Do not use for..." boundaries reduce the composite collision score (0 = ignore boundaries, 1 = fully cancel overlap when scopes are mutually excluded).
skillMdInspector.config.collision.ngramS: Character n-gram size used by the collision character-similarity metric.
skillMdInspector.config.collision.thresh: Composite similarity (0-1) at or above which two skills are reported as a potential collision. The default was lowered from 0.4 to 0.3 when the composite became scope-led: scores are lower across the board, and 0.3 is where the labeled benchmark corpus gives the best precision.
skillMdInspector.config.collision.maxRep: Maximum number of collisions listed in the workspace report and tree view. A workspace whose skills share one house template can produce tens of thousands of pairs; the rest are counted rather than rendered.
skillMdInspector.config.collision.weight: Relative weights blended into the composite collision similarity (normalized to sum to 1). Scope overlap leads because it is the only metric that compares what the skills do rather than how similarly they are worded; the lexical metrics corroborate it. A weights object saved before scopeOverlap existed still works - the missing key takes its default weight.

Weight of scope overlap: how much two skills agree on what they operate on and what they do to it. Omitting this key from a customized weights object keeps the default weight rather than dropping the metric.
skillMdInspector.config.names.similarity: Similarity (0–1) at or above which two different skill names are flagged as confusingly similar. Exact duplicates are always reported.
skillMdInspector.config.heuristics.title: Heuristics
skillMdInspector.config.heuristics.dicti: Acronyms and technology names recognized as concrete artifact or domain evidence.
Explicit surface forms for action verbs. Keys are base verbs and values are recognized forms; explicit entries take precedence over regular morphology.
Base verbs recognized as concrete capabilities in description diagnostics, description completeness, local improvement, and collision features.
High-signal artifact and domain terms used by description quality and collision feature extraction.
Domain terms that make a low-signal artifact such as file, data, code, or document concrete.
Common terms removed before workspace description collision similarity is calculated.

Terms that are both a capability verb and an artifact (for example "test"). A listed term is read as the verb only in a verb position, so "Create unit tests" contributes the artifact and "Test a module" contributes the capability. Every entry must also appear in actionVerbs and in one of the artifact lists.
Phrases that act as both a positive usage trigger and an exclusive boundary.
Terms ignored when deciding whether the opening sentence names a concrete capability object.
Irregular plural normalization used by artifact matching and collision analysis. Keys are singular bases and values are plural forms.
Generic artifact terms that count only when accompanied by an artifact support term.
Multi-word artifact phrases recognized by description quality and collision feature extraction.
Phrases that introduce a negative usage boundary and separate collision scopes.
Conservative phrases that indicate an overbroad skill-selection scope when used in a usage or trigger context.
Phrases that introduce a positive usage-trigger clause.
Non-negative phrases that restrict scope for boundary detection and scoring.
Terms ignored when evaluating whether trigger and boundary clauses contain concrete scope.
Terms that make trigger and boundary clause content too vague to receive full credit.
Ambiguous acronyms that count only when their matched spelling is uppercase.
Words and phrases treated as vague in description diagnostics and description completeness.
Phrases such as only for or limited to that name the skill scope rather than exclude one; they earn boundary credit in scoring but are not collision exclusions.

Capability verbs that count as the same capability when comparing two skills' scope. Keys are group ids and values are the verbs in that group; groups must not share a verb. A verb outside "actionVerbs" is simply never matched.

Artifact terms that count as the same kind of object when comparing two skills' scope (for example spreadsheet, xlsx and workbook). Keys are group ids and values are the terms in that group; groups must not share a term.
skillMdInspector.config.discovery.exclud: Glob patterns for directories to skip when discovering SKILL.md files across the workspace (the tree view and workspace report). Setting this replaces the defaults.
skillMdInspector.config.resources.direct: Relative resource directories monitored for unreferenced bundled files. This replaces the default list; absolute paths and .. traversal are ignored.
skillMdInspector.config.resources.exclud: Glob patterns for files and folders to exclude from resource discovery. Setting this replaces the defaults.
skillMdInspector.config.links.title: Links
skillMdInspector.config.links.onlineChec: Check remote-link availability during full validation. Enabling this sends HTTP requests to URLs referenced by SKILL.md files.
Maximum number of concurrent remote-link requests across one complete validation operation.
skillMdInspector.config.security.title: Security
skillMdInspector.config.security.enabled: Statically scan SKILL.md files for security risks (dangerous/risky commands, risky public services, hardcoded credentials, prompt-injection wording, hidden content, and sensitive-path references). Analysis is local and offline; nothing is executed.
skillMdInspector.config.security.scanRes: Also scan bundled resource files during full validation. Scripts are checked for commands, secrets, risky services, sensitive paths, and invisible Unicode; text resources also receive prompt-injection and hidden-comment checks.
skillMdInspector.config.security.maxScan: Bundled resource files larger than this size (in KiB) are skipped by the security scan.
skillMdInspector.config.security.allowed: Host suffixes to treat as trusted, suppressing risky-service findings (e.g. "internal.example.com").

Known-safe commands that suppress a risky-tier command warning: either the command itself, or the exact line you use it on. Dangerous-tier findings are never suppressed; use severityOverrides for those.
skillMdInspector.config.security.additio: Additional regular expressions (JavaScript syntax) that flag a line as a risky command (warning). Invalid patterns are ignored with a configuration warning.
Additional regular expressions (JavaScript syntax) that flag a line as a dangerous command (error). Invalid patterns are ignored with a configuration warning.
Additional host suffixes to flag as risky public services (e.g. paste or file-upload endpoints).
skillMdInspector.config.severity.title: Severity
skillMdInspector.config.severityOverride:
Override the severity of diagnostics by code, or disable one with `off` (e.g. `{ "skill.description.vague": "information" }`). Specification errors are protected unless `#skillMdInspector.severity.allowSpecificationOverrides#` is enabled.

[Configure with a picker…](command:skillMdInspector.configureSeverityOverrides)
skillMdInspector.config.severity.allowSp: Allow skillMdInspector.severityOverrides to downgrade or disable specification-level errors (an invalid file). Off by default so structural errors are not hidden accidentally.
skillMdInspector.config.templates.title: Templates
skillMdInspector.config.templates.descri: Custom SKILL.md templates. A non-empty array replaces the bundled templates.
skillMdInspector.config.templates.item.l: Template name displayed in the selection list.
skillMdInspector.config.templates.item.d: Optional explanation displayed in the selection list.
skillMdInspector.config.templates.item.f: YAML frontmatter lines without the opening and closing --- delimiters.
skillMdInspector.config.templates.item.b: Markdown body lines. Use an empty string to insert a blank line.
skillMdInspector.config.views.title: Views
skillMdInspector.config.navigator.additi: Additional local agent roots to show in the Installed Agents view.
skillMdInspector.config.openCode.maxDisc: Maximum OpenCode session JSON files to discover.
skillMdInspector.config.openCode.maxPrev: Maximum characters retained in OpenCode previews.
skillMdInspector.config.openCode.maxSess: Maximum OpenCode session export file size to read, in MiB.
skillMdInspector.config.openCode.scanRec: Scan the selected OpenCode sessions folder recursively.
